title: Verify the committed artifact in a clean checkout
environment: Source handoffs with mixed tracked/untracked changes; clean Python checks do not establish application-runtime acceptance.
goal: Recover and hand off a coherent tested source revision.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Local passing tests were taken as evidence that the committed artifact was self-contained.
what_worked: Historical correction: Recover the specific missing dependency as an atomic change, then validate a fresh HEAD-only checkout with the correct package root. Verification reported by the source: The clean checkout exposed the missing import. After dependency recovery, committed-source imports, the expected test population and compileall passed. Blender/Unity acceptance was not run in this recovery.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: The dirty workspace passed 238 tests while committed source had 172. A first recovery commit still imported parser APIs absent from the commit.
why: Confirmed: required semantic parser APIs remained only in a modified workspace file.
improved_method: Test the exact committed artifact from a clean checkout and reconcile test-population differences. Do not sweep unrelated dirty files into a commit to make local results reproducible.
when_to_use: Source handoffs with mixed tracked/untracked changes; clean Python checks do not establish application-runtime acceptance.
when_not_to_use: Source handoffs with mixed tracked/untracked changes; clean Python checks do not establish application-runtime acceptance.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
